clue.text: Graduate's cigarette-end on a musical instrument

parts.note: a graduate holds a BA, Bachelor of Arts, and the 's is kept as S
the stub is what is left of a smoked cigarette

explanation.surface: A graduate puffs a cigarette while playing in a band.
explanation.definitionFit: A bass tuba is the large low-pitched brass instrument, an example of a musical instrument.

clue.text: The woman's daughter and Edward treated like cattle?

parts.note: the possessive pronoun for a woman is her
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
Ed is the usual short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A mother complains that her daughter and Edward were treated like livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle are driven together in a group by drovers; the question mark flags that people can be handled that way too.

clue.text: Blue vehicle, turning over, last in rally

indicators.note: a vehicle turning over in a crash suits a word being read backwards

parts.note: a car is the everyday vehicle

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the word rally

explanation.surface: A car flips over at the end of a motor rally.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue in the sense of risqué or smutty is a synonym for suggestive, near-the-knuckle humour.

clue.text: Composed a steed that's excited

indicators.note: an excited horse is agitated and jumbled, so the letters of the phrase are stirred up

explanation.surface: A rider stays composed on a horse that is getting excited.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed means calm and unhurried, a synonym of quietly dignified.

clue.text: English queen falls in Africa

definitions.meaning: the great waterfall on the Zambezi between Zambia and Zimbabwe bears this name

explanation.surface: An English queen takes a tumble while travelling in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one name: the long-reigning nineteenth-century monarch, and the Zambezi waterfall named after her by Livingstone.

clue.text: Relatives transporting Liam into outskirts of Fowey

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
the outskirts are the edges, so take the first and last letters of the word Fowey
transporting can mean carrying away in a rapture, which shakes the letters of the name Liam about

explanation.surface: Relatives are driving Liam into the edge of a Cornish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transporting' reads as giving Liam a lift, but it means carrying away in rapture, so it signals the rearrangement (AMIL); Fowey is a small harbour town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A family is a group of people related to one another, so it collectively means relatives.

clue.text: Yours truly on lake

parts.note: a jokey way for a speaker to refer to themselves, so me
re means on or about, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: Someone signs off a postcard sent from a lakeside holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a poetic or regional word for a small lake or pond.

clue.text: Mean to declare silver necklace ultimately

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word necklace

explanation.surface: Someone means to announce that a necklace is silver after all.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean of a set of values is the arithmetic midpoint, a synonym in statistics.

clue.text: Informant inside that is angry

indicators.note: says the informer's word sits within the letters for that is

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
a rat is slang for someone who tells tales to the authorities

explanation.surface: A mole inside the organisation is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Irate is a straightforward synonym for furious or cross.

clue.text: Unfortunately, promotion is obtained by cunning

indicators.note: the promotion is held by, so taken inside, the cunning word

parts.note: sly means crafty or cunning
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: Someone regrets that a promotion at work came through underhand scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly used as a sentence adverb means regrettably, a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Old Hollywood actor moving east to absorb atmosphere

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something in, so one piece goes inside the other
moving shifts the letters of the word east into a new order

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: A veteran film star relocates eastward to soak up the local ambience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving east' looks like a relocation, but 'moving' scrambles the compass word (to ASTE) and 'to absorb' takes the atmosphere inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the dancing star of 1930s and 1940s Hollywood musicals.

clue.text: Boxers perhaps controlled by sport

parts.note: under, as in under control or under orders
to sport a garment is to wear it

explanation.surface: Boxers are kept under control by the governing body of their sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' looks like fighters, but here they are shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are one example of clothing worn beneath outer garments, hence the perhaps.

clue.text: Italian twitching — he's sentimental about birds

parts.note: a Roman is someone from Rome, so an Italian
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: An Italian birdwatcher is soppy about his feathered friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twitching' suggests birdwatching (twitching in British slang), but it is the muscle spasm; 'birds' is British slang for women.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who gets soppy over women, called birds in British slang, is a sentimental lover of romance.

clue.text: Definitely heads for Yarmouth every summer

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, taken here from three words

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker insists they definitely go to Great Yarmouth, an English seaside resort, every summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes said emphatically is an affirmative, a synonym for certainly as a reply.

clue.text: Diane's arranged to leave US city

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Diane's are put in a new order

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Diane has made plans to depart the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian city on the Pacific coast near Mexico is an example of an American city.

clue.text: Curve seen in sugarcane

indicators.note: says the letters can be seen inside the word sugarcane

explanation.surface: A bend is visible in a stalk of sugarcane.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is part of a circle, so a synonym for a curve.

clue.text: Young reporter is initially mentioning art movement

parts.note: a cub reporter is a trainee journalist

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word mentioning

explanation.surface: A junior journalist is first to mention a new art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism, led by Picasso and Braque, is an example of a twentieth-century school of painting.

clue.text: Thinking there's no time for reconciliation

indicators.note: says one letter is absent from the thinking word

parts.note: meditation is deep thought

explanation.surface: A negotiator argues there is no time left for patching things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is the process of bringing disputing parties to agreement, so a means of reconciliation.

clue.text: Doctor embraces one with the trembling condition

indicators.note: a doctor embracing something holds it inside the abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A doctor comforts a patient suffering from the shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dither is an agitated state of nervousness, close to a fit of the shakes.

clue.text: Rascal to disclose damage

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to air views is to make them known

explanation.surface: A mischief-maker threatens to reveal something harmful.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or spoil, a synonym of the verb damage.

clue.text: Taxi, one appropriate for a group of politicians

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
I is the Roman numeral one
to net something is to seize or take it, so to appropriate it

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a taxi is the right vehicle for a party of MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' reads as an adjective (suitable) but is the verb meaning take.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is the senior body of government ministers, an example of a group of politicians.

clue.text: One in pack is an eccentric

definitions.meaning: a single item from a deck of fifty-two for playing games
an amusingly odd person, a character

explanation.surface: One member of the gang is a bit of an oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a playing piece from a deck and, informally, a comic or quirky person.

clue.text: Top trip, without limits, somewhere in the Gulf of Naples

definitions.text: somewhere in the Gulf of Naples

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: dropping the limits leaves the inner letters of the word trip

explanation.surface: A first-rate trip with no restrictions takes a tourist around the Bay of Naples.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is the island off the Sorrento peninsula, an example of a place in that bay.

clue.text: Reportedly vintage rowing team

indicators.note: says the word is as heard, not as written

parts.note: a cru is a French term for a wine-growing estate or vintage

explanation.surface: A veteran boat team is said to be classic.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew is the set of rowers in a boat, a synonym for a rowing team.

clue.text: Holy man in Republic of Ireland finding potato-based food

indicators.note: the saint goes in the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: ROI is the standard abbreviation for the Republic of Ireland
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A saint in Ireland finds something made of potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a cake, an example of a potato dish.

clue.text: Non-daytime ironing?

definitions.meaning: the part of the day after daylight ends
ironing flattens, making a surface smooth and level

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the time after daylight and also, read as even-ing, the act of smoothing flat.
